segments.sec: Start Here: AI Basics
segments.say: Lesson 1. A I, M L, Deep Learning & GenAI. What each term actually means, how machine learning differs from normal programming, and how a model "learns" from examples.

segments.sec: The basics
segments.say: A I is the broad goal of making computers do things that seem intelligent. Machine learning (M L) is the main way we do it today: instead of writing rules by hand, we show the computer lots of examples and it learns the pattern itself. Here is an analogy. Teaching a child to recognise dogs: you don't give them a rulebook ("four legs, fur, tail. "). You point at many dogs and say "dog". Eventually they recognise dogs they've never seen. That's machine learning.

segments.sec: The basics
segments.say: Why does this matter? Every A I-engineering interview assumes you can explain these terms precisely. L L Ms, rag and agents all sit on top of these ideas. A few key words. Artificial Intelligence: Any technique that makes machines act smart (even hand-written rules). Machine Learning: Learning patterns from data instead of hand-coding rules. Deep Learning: M L using large neural networks with many layers. Generative A I: Models that create new content: text, images, code, audio. Model: The learned "function" that turns inputs into outputs. Training: Showing examples and adjusting the model until it's accurate. Inference: Using the trained model to make predictions.

segments.sec: Watch: How the terms fit together
segments.say: How the terms fit together. A I is the big umbrella: any program that acts "smart". A chess bot with hand-written rules counts, even though it never learns.

segments.sec: Watch: How the terms fit together
segments.say: Machine learning is the part of A I that learns from data. A spam filter sees thousands of emails labelled spam / not-spam and learns which word patterns matter.

segments.sec: Watch: How the terms fit together
segments.say: Deep learning is M L with big neural networks (many layers). It's what made images, speech and language work well from about 2012 onwards.

segments.sec: Watch: How the terms fit together
segments.say: Generative A I is deep learning that creates new content. Large language models (L L Ms) like Claude and G P T generate text and code. That's the focus of this app.

segments.sec: Watch: Normal programming vs machine learning
segments.say: Normal programming versus machine learning. Normal programming: you write the rules ("if the email contains 'lottery', mark it spam"), feed in data, and get answers. Rules break whenever the world changes.

segments.sec: Watch: Normal programming vs machine learning
segments.say: Machine learning flips it: you provide data and the correct answers (labels), for example 10,000 emails each marked spam or not.

segments.sec: Watch: Normal programming vs machine learning
segments.say: Training finds the rules automatically. The output is a model, which you then use on new data. Using it is called inference.

segments.sec: Watch: Watch a tiny model learn (price = w × size)
segments.say: Watch a tiny model learn (price equals w times size). Training data: 3 houses with their real prices. Our model is the simplest possible: price equals w times size. We need to learn the number w (a "weight").

segments.sec: Watch: Watch a tiny model learn (price = w × size)
segments.say: Start with a random guess, w equals 2. The predictions are way too low. The gap between guess and truth is the loss.

segments.sec: Watch: Watch a tiny model learn (price = w × size)
segments.say: Nudge w in the direction that reduces the error leads to w equals 4. Closer.

segments.sec: Watch: Watch a tiny model learn (price = w × size)
segments.say: w equals 5 leads to perfect. That's training: repeatedly adjust weights to shrink the loss.

segments.sec: Watch: Watch a tiny model learn (price = w × size)
segments.say: Inference: use the learned w on a house it has never seen. Real models learn billions of weights at once instead of one.

segments.sec: Learn
segments.say: Three ways machines learn. Supervised: learn from labelled examples (email leads to spam?). Covers classification (pick a category) and regression (predict a number). Unsupervised: find structure without labels: clustering customers, grouping similar tickets. Reinforcement learning: learn by trial and reward: games, robotics, and the R L H F step that makes chatbots helpful.

segments.sec: Learn
segments.say: Words you will hear constantly. Features: the input signals (size, location). Label: the correct answer in training data. Parameters / weights: the numbers the model learns. Train / validation / test split: learn on one part, tune on another, report on unseen data. Overfitting: memorising the training data instead of learning the pattern, so it fails on new data.

segments.sec: Learn
segments.say: Say it in the interview. "A I is the umbrella; machine learning learns patterns from data instead of hand-written rules; deep learning does that with large neural networks; and generative A I, including L L Ms, uses deep learning to create new content. Training adjusts the parameters to minimise a loss on examples; inference applies the trained model to new inputs.".

segments.sec: Compare
segments.say: Let's compare. A I: any "smart" behaviour, rule-based chess engine. Machine learning: learns patterns from data, spam filter, fraud detection. Deep learning: M L with big neural networks, face recognition, speech-to-text. Generative A I: creates new content, Claude, G P T, image generators. L L M: generative model for text, summarise, chat, write code.

segments.sec: Compare
segments.say: Types of learning. Supervised: inputs plus correct labels, predict ticket priority. Unsupervised: inputs only, cluster similar alerts. Reinforcement: actions plus rewards, game A I, R L H F.

segments.sec: Interview recall
segments.say: A likely interview question: Explain A I versus M L versus deep learning versus GenAI in 30 seconds. A strong answer: A I is any smart behaviour. M L is A I that learns from data. Deep learning is M L with large neural networks. Generative A I is deep learning that creates content, like L L Ms generating text.
